text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Several species of dead fish are being washed up on beaches along the Namibian coast apparently affected by a red tide.
- Hospitals in northern Namibia are short of blood stocks because people are refusing to donate blood for fear of being affected by the HIV virus.

- A double veterinary cordon of cattle and game fences in northern Botswana has reached 147 kilometres between the Okavango, south of the Mahango game park, and the Kwando river in the eastern Caprivi. The fence is said to be dangerous as it blocks major migratory routes of large game species.

- The Namibian National Students Organisation has joined the ranks of those asking for a third term of office for President Sam Nujoma, saying every political party has the right to nominate its presidential candidate.
